It excludes changes inherited only through `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, `BackboneElement`, and `Extension`; those are listed out of scope and should be handled by their assigned reports. Related core SearchParameter instance files were sampled only to estimate prevalence of the local schema changes, not to report per-parameter changes.

narrativeReportMd:
# SearchParameter R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes found. The most important R4-to-R6 breaks are removal of `xpath`/`xpathUsage`, the new requirement that `expression` be accompanied by `processingMode`, new hard constraints on `comparator` and `code`, and required-binding changes for `modifier`, `type`, `base`, and `target`.

## Scope
The R4 and R6 `SearchParameter` StructureDefinitions are the same canonical artifact and remain concrete resources based on `DomainResource`. This report covers local SearchParameter fields and directly bound terminology. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, `BackboneElement`, and `Extension` changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
R6 moves SearchParameter away from XPath metadata and toward explicit FHIRPath processing. It also tightens URL/search syntax rules and expands or changes several required code domains. R6 adds optional canonical metadata and conditional applicability information that R4 cannot represent without extensions.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `SearchParameter.xpath`/`xpathUsage` removal, `expression` requiring `processingMode`, `modifier` code rename/expansion, and the `base`/`target` resource-type binding change. These affect validation, generated models, search-parameter registries, and server/client conformance discovery.

## Findings requiring human review
Manual review is most important for XPath-to-FHIRPath migration, missing or newly introduced resource-type codes in `base`/`target`, R6-only conditional `constraint`, and semantic chain declarations.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most hard breaks could have been softened with deprecated optional fields, warning-first constraints, or temporary deprecated terminology aliases. R6 nevertheless improves explicit machine-processable search metadata and safer URL semantics.

## Follow-up analysis
Use the base artifact reports for inherited resource/element behavior. Use resource-specific reports and terminology expansions to decide how SearchParameters on removed or renamed resource types should be mapped, retired, or preserved with extensions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 keeps the `SearchParameter` artifact identity but introduces several local hard validation breaks. Top concerns are loss of XPath fields, mandatory `processingMode` for expressions, changed required code domains, and resource-type binding differences; the main uncertainty is exact terminology-expansion behavior for version-independent resource types.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat SearchParameter definitions as executable conformance metadata, not passive documentation. Bulk transforms need to remove XPath fields, populate `processingMode`, rename `ofType` to `of-type`, validate `base`/`target` resource codes, update generated enum sets, and preserve R6-only metadata through extensions when downgrading to R4.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local element, cardinality, type, constraint, and binding deltas because both StructureDefinitions and local CodeSystems were available. Confidence is medium for exact resource-type binding impact because no external terminology expansion service or official cross-version ConceptMap was used.

findings.title: SearchParameter.xpath and SearchParameter.xpathUsage were removed in R6

oldState.summary: R4 allowed optional XPath extraction metadata and required xpathUsage when xpath was present.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local CodeSystem comparison shows `normal`, `phonetic`, and `other` continue conceptually in R6 `processingMode`, while R4 XPath-specific spatial modes `nearby` and `distance` have no R6 processing-mode code.

constraints.human: If an xpath is present, there SHALL be an xpathUsage

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a SearchParameter could carry an XPath expression in `xpath` and describe how that XPath should be interpreted using `xpathUsage`.

newState.summary: R6 has no xpath or xpathUsage elements; the remaining local processing hint is processingMode for FHIRPath expression results.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 `processingMode` is not a full syntactic replacement for XPath; it classifies how FHIRPath `expression` results are processed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 SearchParameter instances must not contain `xpath` or `xpathUsage`. Systems that still depend on XPath expressions need an extension or external migration policy.

facts.oldValue: 1340 of 1400 local R4 SearchParameter resources contained xpath; 1399 contained xpathUsage
facts.note: Counted in the supplied R4 package.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `processingMode` inherits three code meanings from `xpathUsage`, but it is tied to `expression`, not an XPath string. This is a replacement only for the processing-classification aspect, not for the removed XPath expression itself.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format break for R4 instances containing `xpath` or `xpathUsage`: those element names are absent from the R6 StructureDefinition. The prevalence is high in the supplied R4 core package, where most core SearchParameter examples carry XPath metadata. R6-to-R4 conversion is also lossy because R6 `processingMode` has no R4 element unless mapped back to `xpathUsage` with an invented or unavailable XPath.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Search indexing and conformance publication can be business-critical; losing XPath extraction metadata can change server indexing behavior even though it is not direct clinical data.

justification.inferredGoal: Move SearchParameter definitions away from XPath-specific extraction toward FHIRPath-based extraction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep optional deprecated `xpath` and `xpathUsage` alongside `processingMode` for a transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving SearchParameter definitions toward FHIRPath and away from XPath is a reasonable R6 goal. Keeping the R4 XPath fields would preserve many old instances, but it would also require base R6 validators and tooling to keep supporting XML-centric extraction metadata and the R4 spatial modes that do not cleanly map to `processingMode`. Because that tradeoff is material, the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would retain `xpath` and `xpathUsage` as deprecated optional elements while adding `processingMode`, with warnings discouraging new XPath use. This would preserve most R4 SearchParameter registries during migration, but it would leave two extraction representations in the base resource and could make deprecated XPath content persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy registries but leaves XML/XPath semantics and duplicate extraction metadata in base R6.

evidence.detail: R4 defines SearchParameter.xpath as 0..1 string.
R4 defines SearchParameter.xpathUsage as 0..1 code bound required to search-xpath-usage.
R6 has no SearchParameter.xpath or SearchParameter.xpathUsage element; it adds SearchParameter.processingMode.
R4 xpathUsage codes `nearby` and `distance` are not present in R6 search-processingmode.
Local package count found 1340 R4 SearchParameter resources with xpath and 1399 with xpathUsage.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is lossless only when the XPath duplicated the FHIRPath expression and `xpathUsage` can be mapped to an R6 `processingMode` code. XPath-only behavior, especially spatial usage, needs manual review or an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: `xpath` and `xpathUsage` disappeared from the R6 SearchParameter resource. R4 publishers that still include the XPath representation will fail strict R6 validation, and systems that used XPath as the executable extraction language cannot recover that behavior from `processingMode` alone.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 SearchParameter with `xpath` or `xpathUsage` is structurally invalid in R6 because those elements are not defined. R6-to-R4: `processingMode` can sometimes be mapped to R4 `xpathUsage`, but R6 has no XPath string to populate, and R4 `nearby`/`distance` values have no R6 counterpart.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Remove `xpath` and `xpathUsage` for R6 output. Confirm each SearchParameter has an equivalent FHIRPath `expression`; if not, create an implementation-specific extension or retire the parameter. For migrated parameters that used `normal`, `phonetic`, or `other`, map to `processingMode`; for `nearby` or `distance`, require manual review because the R6 processing-mode binding has no equivalent.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same modernization goal could have been achieved with optional deprecated XPath fields or a standard extension. That would have allowed old SearchParameter registries to validate while tooling migrated to FHIRPath. The cost would be keeping legacy XPath semantics visible in the core resource longer.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The local R4 core package shows this is a common break for core SearchParameter instances, not just an obscure extension point.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 SearchParameter definitions commonly carry `xpath` and `xpathUsage`, while R6 removes both elements and expects the FHIRPath-oriented `processingMode` model instead. A registry, validator, or generated model that accepts many R4 core SearchParameter resources would reject or drop those fields in R6. This is conformance metadata rather than patient data, but it directly affects search indexing definitions and publication of server capabilities.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has `SearchParameter.xpath` 0..1 string and `SearchParameter.xpathUsage` 0..1 code; R6 StructureDefinition has neither element and adds `SearchParameter.processingMode`.
Local R4 core package count: 1340 SearchParameter resources with `xpath` and 1399 with `xpathUsage`.
R4 `search-xpath-usage` includes `nearby` and `distance`; R6 `search-processingmode` has only `normal`, `phonetic`, and `other`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: SearchParameter is FMM 3 trial-use, so broad breakage in mature search conformance metadata carries meaningful stability pressure, though not a normative freeze.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing `xpath` or `xpathUsage` use element names absent from the R6 base resource; generated models and validators may reject them, and R6-to-R4 conversion cannot recover an XPath from `processingMode` alone.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking R6 base design would retain `xpath` and `xpathUsage` as deprecated optional elements while preferring `expression` and `processingMode`. The tradeoff is keeping obsolete XML/XPath extraction metadata and duplicate ways to describe processing.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the fresh review gives the deprecated-field alternative enough weight to warrant Revisit.

findings.title: R6 requires processingMode whenever expression is present

oldState.summary: R4 expression was optional and did not require a processing-mode element.

constraints.human: If an xpath is present, there SHALL be an xpathUsage

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 tied the local paired-field invariant to `xpath`, not to `expression`.

newState.summary: R6 expression remains optional, but if present then processingMode must also be present.

constraints.human: If an expression is present, there SHALL be a processingMode

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes the processing classification mandatory for every SearchParameter that declares a FHIRPath `expression`.

facts.oldValue: If an xpath is present, there SHALL be an xpathUsage
facts.newValue: If an expression is present, there SHALL be a processingMode

facts.oldValue: 1384 of 1400 local R4 SearchParameter resources had expression with no processingMode

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same invariant key `spd-1` was reused, but its dependent fields changed from the removed XPath pair to the FHIRPath expression/processingMode pair.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break independent of the removed XPath fields: an R4 SearchParameter with a valid `expression` but no `processingMode` satisfies R4 but violates R6 `spd-1`. The supplied R4 core package contains this pattern for most SearchParameter resources.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: SearchParameter registries and conformance generation may fail en masse until processing modes are populated.

justification.inferredGoal: Require SearchParameter publishers to state how FHIRPath expression results should be processed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `processingMode` optional with missing meaning `normal`, plus a warning to populate it explicitly.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring publishers to state how FHIRPath expression results are processed is a sound goal, especially after XPath removal. The hard R6 error is probably avoidable, however, because absent `processingMode` could have been given a normative default of `normal` or treated as a best-practice warning. That alternative would preserve existing R4 instances while still allowing R6 authors and validators to prefer explicit processing modes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative is to define missing `processingMode` as `normal` and warn when it is omitted. Systems needing `phonetic` or `other` could still populate it explicitly. The tradeoff is that some legacy parameters with non-normal implementation behavior might be under-specified until reviewed, but this is a moderate migration risk rather than a reason old base instances must fail validation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Less explicit and may hide unusual processing, but avoids mass invalidation without duplicate fields.

evidence.detail: R4 spd-1 only required xpathUsage when xpath existed.
R6 spd-1 requires processingMode when expression exists.
Local package count found 1384 R4 SearchParameter resources with expression and no processingMode.

examples.examplesMd: Most straightforward migrations will populate `processingMode: "normal"`, but parameters that relied on special text, phonetic, or non-standard extraction behavior should not be bulk-defaulted without review.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 turns the processing classification for a FHIRPath expression into a required companion value. This will surprise migrations that simply drop R4 XPath fields and keep the existing `expression` unchanged: the result still fails R6 unless `processingMode` is added.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: any R4 SearchParameter with `expression` and no `processingMode` violates R6 `spd-1`. This does not create a major R6-to-R4 wire-format problem beyond the fact that R4 does not know `processingMode`; the validation break is primarily R4-to-R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Add `processingMode` for every R6 SearchParameter with `expression`. Use `normal` only when the expression directly yields indexed values. Use `phonetic` or `other` where the old definition or implementation behavior indicates special processing. Add tests that validate migrated resources against `spd-1`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A default of `normal` would have made old instances continue to validate, but the R6 design favors explicit declaration. The safer migration stance is not to assume all legacy expressions are normal without checking old `xpathUsage`, parameter type, and implementation notes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 turns `processingMode` into a required companion whenever `expression` is present. Most R4 core SearchParameter resources have an `expression` but no `processingMode`, so a straightforward R4 registry import becomes invalid even when the intended processing is ordinary FHIRPath extraction. The goal of making processing semantics explicit is reasonable, but the hard error appears avoidable.
keyEvidence: R4 invariant `spd-1` is `xpath.empty() or xpathUsage.exists()`.
R6 invariant `spd-1` is `expression.empty() or processingMode.exists()`.
Local R4 core package count: 1384 SearchParameter resources have `expression` and no `processingMode`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 trial-use raises the burden for invalidating almost the whole R4 core SearchParameter catalog for a new explicitness requirement.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 SearchParameter with `expression` and no `processingMode` passes R4 but violates an R6 error invariant.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could make absent `processingMode` mean `normal` and add a warning or best-practice rule encouraging explicit values. The tradeoff is that unusual legacy behavior might remain under-specified until reviewed, but that is less disruptive than a mass validation failure.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Yes alternative judgment.

findings.title: R6 forbids comparator unless type is number, date, quantity, or special

oldState.summary: R4 allowed comparator values on the element without a local invariant restricting SearchParameter.type.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 comparator code set was required, but the SearchParameter StructureDefinition did not say that only certain search types could carry comparator declarations.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same comparator code set but adds error invariant spd-3 limiting the declaring parameter types.

constraints.human: Search parameters comparator can only be used on type 'number', 'date', 'quantity' or 'special'.

newState.narrativeMd: A SearchParameter of type `string`, `token`, `reference`, `composite`, `uri`, or `resource` cannot declare `comparator` in R6.

facts.note: No comparator codes were added or removed in the local CodeSystem comparison.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The break comes from the new invariant, not from the comparator terminology. A previously valid R4 instance such as a token SearchParameter advertising `eq` now fails R6 validation because the containing type is not one of the allowed comparator types.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect comparator metadata can cause clients to issue unsupported search queries; the risk is operational rather than direct clinical content loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Align SearchParameter metadata with search semantics where comparators apply only to ordered or special value domains.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce the comparator/type rule first as a warning or best-practice invariant.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 rule matches the core search semantics: comparators only make sense for ordered or special search domains. A warning-first rule would be less disruptive, but it would still allow base-conformant metadata that clients could reasonably misread as comparator support for unordered types. Given the semantic correctness of the rule and apparently low core prevalence, the hard invariant is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking design would keep `comparator` valid on all types for one release and emit a warning when `type` is not `number`, `date`, `quantity`, or `special`. That preserves old instances, but it weakens conformance and leaves unsafe capability metadata available to clients.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves rare legacy instances but keeps misleading comparator declarations formally valid.

evidence.detail: R6 adds an error invariant restricting comparator by SearchParameter.type.
R4 has the comparator element and required binding but no equivalent local type restriction.
The comparator codes themselves are unchanged between the supplied CodeSystems.
Local package count found one R4 core SearchParameter (`example`) with comparator on a token parameter.

examples.examplesMd: For non-ordered types, remove `comparator` rather than trying to map it to another field.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a semantic validation rule that comparators are only valid for ordered or special search types. This is likely correct semantically, but it is still a hard validation change for any legacy SearchParameter registry that advertised comparators on token, string, reference, composite, URI, or resource parameters.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: a R4 SearchParameter with `type: "token"` and `comparator: ["eq"]` is rejected by R6 `spd-3`. R6-to-R4 is not a problem because R4 can syntactically carry the same comparator list.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit all SearchParameter definitions with `comparator`. Keep comparator only when `type` is `number`, `date`, `quantity`, or `special`; otherwise remove it and update conformance/capability tests to verify clients do not infer comparator support.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The least-breaking alternative would have been a warning invariant, but a hard invariant better protects clients from relying on nonsensical comparator declarations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds an error invariant limiting `comparator` to numeric, date, quantity, and special search parameters. That can invalidate an R4 definition that advertised a comparator for a token or other non-ordered type, but the pattern appears rare in the core package and the rule prevents misleading capability metadata that could cause clients to send unsupported queries.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition constraint `spd-3`: `comparator.empty() or (type in ('number' | 'date' | 'quantity' | 'special'))`.
R4 has `SearchParameter.comparator` with the same required comparator code set but no equivalent type restriction.
Local R4 core package count found one disallowed pattern: SearchParameter `example`, type `token`, comparator `eq`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 makes the validation break worth noticing, but the narrow prevalence and conformance-quality rationale make the break proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a previously valid SearchParameter can fail R6 validation if it lists comparators on an unsupported `type`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have introduced this as a warning-level invariant for one release. That would preserve rare legacy instances, but it would also keep misleading comparator declarations formally valid in base conformance metadata.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment.

findings.title: R6 rejects SearchParameter.code values containing '.', '$', '|', or whitespace

oldState.summary: R4 required a code but had only compatibility guidance to use lowercase ASCII.

semanticText.comment: For maximum compatibility, use only lowercase ASCII characters.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not define a local error invariant forbidding separator characters in SearchParameter.code.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant spd-4 forbidding '.', '$', '|', and whitespace in code.

constraints.human: Search parameter codes SHALL NOT contain '.', '$', '|', or whitespace characters

semanticText.comment: For maximum compatibility, use only lowercase ASCII characters and hyphens. The characters '.', '$', '|' and whitespace are prohibited as they are used as separators in search parameter processing.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes separator avoidance a formal validation rule because those characters participate in search URL parsing.

facts.oldValue: For maximum compatibility, use only lowercase ASCII characters.
facts.newValue: For maximum compatibility, use only lowercase ASCII characters and hyphens; '.', '$', '|', and whitespace are prohibited.

facts.oldValue: 0 of 1400 local R4 SearchParameter resources had a code matching the newly forbidden characters
facts.note: Custom registries may still be affected.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard validation break for any old instance using a separator character in `code`. It appears rare in core R4 content, but custom SearchParameter definitions sometimes use dotted or namespaced codes and would need renaming.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is search URL interoperability and registry migration, not clinical data loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Prevent ambiguity with search URL syntax and chained/modifier separators.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep legacy `code` values temporarily and add a distinct URL-safe name or warning rule.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Forbidding `.`, `$`, `|`, and whitespace directly supports unambiguous FHIR search URL parsing, so the goal is strong. A less-breaking design could preserve legacy codes and introduce a separate safe URL name, but that would duplicate the central naming fact and make it less clear which value clients should use. The hard R6 rule is therefore probably justified despite the partial alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would leave `code` unconstrained for older definitions and add a new constrained URL-safe element or warning-level rule. That would preserve old custom codes, but it would split the parameter identity between two fields and could allow unsafe names to remain in registries indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids invalidating unusual names but creates ambiguous primary versus URL-safe parameter names.

evidence.detail: R4 comment only recommends lowercase ASCII for compatibility.
R6 adds an error invariant forbidding separator and whitespace characters in code.
Local package count found no core R4 SearchParameter.code values containing the newly forbidden characters.

examples.examplesMd: The example uses `aliasCode` as an R6 compatibility signal, but clients still need to use the R6-safe `code` as the recommended URL parameter name.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes SearchParameter code hygiene from guidance to a hard constraint. This can break custom definitions that used dots or other separators to create namespaces, even though the same lexical value fit the primitive `code` type in R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: `code: "example.code"` is invalid in R6 because it fails `spd-4`. R6-to-R4 is syntactically safe for valid R6 codes because R4 accepts the narrower code shape.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename invalid codes to lowercase ASCII plus hyphens or another separator-free convention. Publish aliases in `aliasCode` where appropriate, update CapabilityStatement search parameter names, and test URL parsing for chained and modified search parameters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping old codes and adding a URL-safe alias would have minimized validation breakage, but it would leave ambiguous parameter names in the primary code field. The R6 design chooses safer parsing over preserving unusual code names.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 makes separator-safe SearchParameter codes a hard rule by forbidding `.`, `$`, `|`, and whitespace. This is a real validation break for custom R4 definitions that used dotted, namespaced, or otherwise unsafe codes, but no such core R4 SearchParameter codes were found locally and the prohibited characters have direct meaning in FHIR search URL syntax.
keyEvidence: R4 `SearchParameter.code` comment only recommends lowercase ASCII for compatibility.
R6 constraint `spd-4` requires `code.matches('^[^.\\$\\|\\s]+$')`.
Local R4 core package count found no SearchParameter `code` values containing the newly prohibited characters.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 supports caring about custom registry migration, but the low observed prevalence and URL-syntax rationale reduce the need for standards rework.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 SearchParameter with a separator or whitespace in `code` can become invalid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-only rule or a separate URL-safe-name element would preserve unusual legacy codes. The tradeoff is splitting the parameter identity or allowing ambiguous URL names to remain base-valid, which undermines the R6 parsing goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment.

findings.title: Search modifier code ofType was renamed to of-type and new modifier codes were added

oldState.summary: R4 modifier was required-bound to search-modifier-code with code ofType.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem comparison found `ofType` in R4 and no `ofType` in R6.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used camel-case `ofType` for the identifier type modifier.

newState.summary: R6 binding points to search-modifier-all-codes and the underlying search-modifier-code CodeSystem contains of-type plus code-text, text-advanced, and iterate.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 ValueSet also includes an unscoped include in `search-modifier-all-codes`; without a terminology server this report relies on the local complete CodeSystem for concrete added codes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses hyphenated `of-type` and adds new modifier capabilities. Required binding means old `ofType` is no longer valid.

facts.oldValue: Text searches CodeableConcept.text, Coding.display, or Identifier.type.text.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `ofType` and `of-type` have the same display and definition in the local CodeSystems, so this is best treated as a code rename rather than a semantic replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because `SearchParameter.modifier` has a required binding, a R4 instance listing `ofType` becomes invalid in R6. Conversely, R6 instances listing `of-type`, `code-text`, `text-advanced`, or `iterate` cannot be represented as valid R4 SearchParameter.modifier values. Generated enum switches and clients that compare literal modifier codes are especially exposed.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect modifier metadata can change client query construction and server conformance behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize modifier code spelling and expand the modifier vocabulary for newer search behavior.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `ofType` as a deprecated alias while preferring `of-type` and adding the new R6 modifiers.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding new modifier codes and preferring hyphenated spelling are reasonable R6 goals. The hard rejection of the old `ofType` code is not clearly justified by the supplied evidence because the same semantic goal could be met by retaining `ofType` as deprecated with a map to `of-type`. The alternative has real interoperability costs, so it is partial rather than a clean yes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would include both `ofType` and `of-type` in the required R6 value set, mark `ofType` deprecated, and publish a ConceptMap or canonicalization rule. This would preserve R4-valid SearchParameter instances while guiding systems to the R6 spelling. The tradeoff is a long-lived dual spelling for a URL-level modifier, which can complicate enum generation, equality checks, and server/client expectations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 metadata but leaves two spellings for the same modifier and complicates canonical comparisons.

evidence.detail: R4 modifier is required-bound to search-modifier-code|4.0.1.
R6 modifier is required-bound to search-modifier-all-codes|6.0.0-ballot4.
R4 contains `ofType`; R6 contains `of-type`, `code-text`, `text-advanced`, and `iterate`.

examples.examplesMd: `ofType` to `of-type` is a deterministic spelling migration. New R6-only modifier codes require either loss, extension, or profile-specific conversion when producing R4.

findings.narrativeMd: The required modifier vocabulary changed materially. The most obvious break is the camel-case to hyphenated spelling change for `ofType`; R6 also introduces modifier semantics that old R4 validators and generated enums do not know.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: `modifier: ["ofType"]` fails the R6 required binding. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: `of-type`, `code-text`, `text-advanced`, and `iterate` are not valid R4 modifier codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `ofType` to `of-type` during R4-to-R6 migration. For R6-to-R4, preserve R6-only modifier declarations in an extension or reject/down-convert with documented loss. Update enum definitions, query-builder tests, and conformance comparison logic to accept the new spelling and added codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rename was probably avoidable as a hard break by keeping `ofType` in the R6 ValueSet as deprecated. The added codes are naturally R6-only, but the old spelling could have been retained without changing semantics.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A formal ConceptMap would improve confidence for the `ofType` to `of-type` migration, although the local CodeSystem definitions strongly indicate a rename.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required modifier binding changes the `ofType` code to `of-type` while also adding new modifier codes. The additive codes are not a backward break, but removing the R4 spelling means R4 conformance metadata or search behavior that advertises `:ofType` no longer validates against the R6 required value set. Because modifier names are part of the public search API surface, this looks like a spelling cleanup with a direct compatibility cost.
keyEvidence: R4 `SearchParameter.modifier` is required-bound to `search-modifier-code|4.0.1`; R6 binds to `search-modifier-all-codes|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R4 modifier CodeSystem includes `ofType`; R6 modifier CodeSystem includes `of-type`, `code-text`, `text-advanced`, and `iterate`.
Local R4 core SearchParameter resources did not list `ofType`, but the code remains part of the R4 required modifier domain and search URL convention.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 trial-use and the centrality of SearchParameter modifier codes to search interoperability increase the burden for a required-code rename.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 metadata listing `ofType` fails the R6 required binding, and clients or servers comparing generated modifier enums or URL modifiers must handle a renamed code.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could include both `ofType` and `of-type` in the required value set, mark `ofType` deprecated, and publish canonicalization guidance. The tradeoff is dual spellings for one modifier, but that is a familiar transitional burden and seems lower cost than rejecting the old spelling outright.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the fresh review treats the alias alternative as strong enough to justify Revisit.

findings.title: SearchParameter.type added R6-only code resource

oldState.summary: R4 SearchParameter.type required binding had nine codes and no resource code.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 type values were number, date, string, token, reference, composite, quantity, uri, and special.

newState.summary: R6 SearchParameter.type adds resource for search parameters that chain into embedded resources.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local complete CodeSystems show `resource` as the only added search-param-type code.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 defines `resource` as a search parameter type for chaining through embedded resources.

facts.newValue: 2 of 1273 local R6 SearchParameter resources used type=resource

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a widening for R4-to-R6, so old R4 instances do not become invalid because of this change. The break is for generated enums and R6-to-R4 conversion: a valid R6 `type: "resource"` is outside the R4 required binding.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is interoperability for conformance resources and search implementation metadata.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent a new kind of search parameter that chains through embedded resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; R6 widens the `type` value set and preserves R4-to-R6 validity.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding `resource` is a standard way to represent new R6 search semantics and does not invalidate any R4 `SearchParameter.type` value. The compatibility concern is that R4 systems and closed enums cannot represent the new R6 code. That is a down-conversion and implementation-update issue, not a backwards-compatible alternative question for an R4-to-R6 break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 validation because the R6 value set is wider. An extension-only representation or lossy mapping to `special` could help old systems consume R6 content, but those are downgrade mitigations rather than base-design alternatives to a breaking change.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The issue is R6-to-R4 downgrade and generated-enum compatibility, not a breaking base R6 design for R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 binds type to search-param-type|4.0.1.
R6 short includes `resource` in the allowed type list.
Local CodeSystem comparison found R6 added `resource` and removed no R4 type codes.
Local package count found two R6 core SearchParameter resources with type=resource: Bundle-composition and Bundle-message.

examples.examplesMd: A downgrade to R4 `special` might keep an instance syntactically valid but loses the standardized R6 `resource` type semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a new search parameter type. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it is important for R4 clients generated with closed enums and for any service that must publish R6 SearchParameter definitions through an R4 endpoint.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: old values remain valid. R6-to-R4: `type: "resource"` fails the R4 required binding and cannot be represented without loss or extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated enum/code lists for SearchParameter.type. For R6-to-R4 export, either reject resource-type SearchParameters, map them to an extension plus a conventional fallback, or document a lossy mapping to `special` if the receiving system can tolerate it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding an optional extension rather than a base code would have been more backward-compatible but would make the new semantics less discoverable and less interoperable for R6 search tooling.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens `SearchParameter.type` by adding `resource`. No R4 type code is removed, so this does not make R4 SearchParameter instances invalid in R6. R4-era generated enums and R6-to-R4 conversion need to handle the new code, but that is a forward-feature/downgrade issue rather than a problematic R4-to-R6 break.
keyEvidence: R4 `search-param-type` codes are `number,date,string,token,reference,composite,quantity,uri,special`.
R6 `search-param-type` adds `resource` and removes no R4 type codes.
Local R6 core package has two `type=resource` SearchParameters: `Bundle-composition` and `Bundle-message`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 does not turn an additive value-set widening into a stability concern for R4-to-R6 migration.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 `type=resource` cannot be represented in the R4 required value set, but old R4 instances remain valid with respect to this change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Mapping `resource` to `special` or using an extension would only be a downgrade mitigation and would lose R6 semantics.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact framing; agree that no backwards-compatible alternative is applicable.

findings.title: SearchParameter.base and target changed to a version-independent resource-type binding that is not a simple R4 superset

oldState.summary: R4 base and target were required-bound to resource-types|4.0.1.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Using local package CodeSystems/ValueSet compose, 19 R4 resource-type codes were not present in the R6 version-independent-all-resource-types set.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 SearchParameter definitions identify applicable resource types and reference targets using R4 resource-type codes.

newState.summary: R6 base and target are required-bound to version-independent-all-resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4, including all-resource-types plus fhir-old-types.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 set admits new R6 resource/interface codes and selected old-type codes. The listed added codes are a sample of R6 codes absent from R4; full expansion would require a terminology server.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a broader cross-version-looking binding, but the local package composition still did not include every R4 resource-type code.

facts.field: R4 codes not found in local R6 value set

facts.oldValue: 138 R4 SearchParameter base occurrences and 1530 target occurrences used codes not found in the local R6 version-independent set

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because both elements have required bindings, code-set differences are validation differences. An R4 SearchParameter whose `base` or `target` names a resource type missing from the R6 bound set can become invalid in R6. R6 instances can also name R6-only resource/interface types that an R4 validator does not accept.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: This affects conformance catalogs and client discovery for resources that were removed, renamed, or introduced across versions.

justification.inferredGoal: Let SearchParameter definitions refer to current and selected historical resource-type codes across versions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Include all R4 resource-type codes as inactive or deprecated entries in the version-independent value set with mappings to current replacements.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A version-independent resource-type binding is a reasonable goal, and the local evidence suggests that the R6 value set is not a simple R4 superset. A more compatible value set could preserve R4 codes, but without authoritative expansion and resource-lifecycle mappings it is not possible to tell which exclusions are intentional, necessary, or accidental. The alternative is therefore real but only partial, and the overall justification cannot be fully assessed from the supplied inputs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would include every R4 resource-type code in the R6 version-independent value set, marked inactive or deprecated where appropriate, with ConceptMaps to R6 replacements or retirement guidance. This would reduce hard validation failures for old SearchParameters. The tradeoff is that validators would accept obsolete base or target codes unless profiles, lifecycle metadata, or business rules enforce current-version applicability.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves validation but lets obsolete resource targets remain base-valid unless other rules reject or map them.

evidence.detail: R4 base and target are required-bound to resource-types|4.0.1.
R6 base and target are required-bound to version-independent-all-resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local comparison found 19 R4 resource-type codes not present in the R6 version-independent set and 43 R6 version-independent codes not present in R4.
Local package counts found many R4 SearchParameter base/target occurrences using resource codes absent from the local R6 bound set.

examples.examplesMd: The examples illustrate binding-level compatibility. Whether a specific missing resource type has an R6 replacement is owned by that resource artifact analysis.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource-type domain for `base` and `target` changed in a way that materially affects validation and conversion. The new R6 binding is labelled version-independent, but the local package data does not behave as a pure superset of R4; some R4 resource types are absent, and R6 introduces new resource/interface codes unknown to R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid: `base: ["ChargeItem"]` is valid against R4 resource-types but not present in the local R6 version-independent set. R6-valid/not-R4-representable: R6-only codes such as `ActorDefinition` or `SubscriptionTopic` are outside R4 `resource-types`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Validate SearchParameter.base and target values against the R6 ValueSet before migration. For missing R4 resource codes, consult the corresponding resource removal/rename report and map, retire, or extension-carry the parameter. For R6-to-R4 export, reject or extension-carry SearchParameters that name R6-only resource types. Add terminology tests using the actual value set expansion used by your validator.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A truly version-independent value set containing all R4 codes, with inactive markers and ConceptMaps, would reduce hard breaks. The tradeoff is that validators would accept obsolete codes unless profiles or business rules enforced current-version applicability.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confidence is medium for exact terminology impact because no external terminology expansion service was used. The local package files are clear enough to flag a material risk.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `base` and `target` remain required-bound code elements, but R6 binds them to the version-independent all-resource-types value set rather than the R4 resource-types value set. Local expansion from the supplied package shows this is not a simple superset: several R4 resource codes used by R4 core SearchParameters are absent, so otherwise valid R4 definitions can fail R6 terminology validation. For a value set named version-independent, omissions of R4 resource names deserve standards attention unless explicitly justified.
keyEvidence: R4 `SearchParameter.base` and `SearchParameter.target` are required-bound to `resource-types|4.0.1`.
R6 `SearchParameter.base` and `SearchParameter.target` are required-bound to `version-independent-all-resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4`.
Local compose-based comparison found 19 R4 resource-type codes absent from the R6 version-independent set and 43 R6 version-independent codes absent from R4.
Local R4 SearchParameter resources contain 1668 base/target occurrences using the 19 absent R4 codes.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 trial-use raises stability expectations for broad breaks in search conformance catalogs, especially when the R6 binding appears intended to be cross-version.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 SearchParameters whose `base` or `target` names an absent R4 resource code can fail R6 required-binding validation, affecting capability discovery and generated enums.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design would include all R4 resource-type codes in the version-independent set, marked inactive or deprecated where appropriate with lifecycle mappings. The tradeoff is that base validation would accept obsolete targets unless profiles or lifecycle metadata restrict current-version applicability.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the remaining uncertainty is official terminology expansion/rationale, but the local evidence is sufficient for Revisit.

findings.title: R6 adds SearchParameter.constraint for conditional applicability

oldState.summary: R4 had no local element for a FHIRPath condition controlling SearchParameter applicability.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could express extraction logic in `expression`/`xpath`, but not a separate condition saying when the SearchParameter applies.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional 0..1 string constraint: a FHIRPath expression that defines/sets a complex constraint for when this SearchParameter is applicable.

semanticText.definition: FHIRPath expression that defines/sets a complex constraint for when this SearchParameter is applicable.

newState.narrativeMd: `constraint` can change indexing/applicability even when the primary extraction expression is unchanged.

facts.newValue: 1 of 1273 local R6 SearchParameter resources used constraint

impact.impactRationaleMd: This optional addition does not invalidate R4 instances in R6. It creates a representability and runtime risk in the reverse direction: an R4 system can syntactically ignore the unknown element, but then may index or advertise a SearchParameter outside the condition intended by R6.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If ignored, conditional search applicability can change query results for affected resources.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent complex applicability rules that cannot be captured by a single extraction expression.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; this optional R6 element does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The optional `constraint` element fills a real expressivity gap for conditional SearchParameter applicability and does not create an R4-to-R6 validation break. Its compatibility issue is that older R4 systems cannot represent or execute the new metadata without extensions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the element is optional and additive, there is no backwards-compatible alternative needed to preserve R4 instances in R6. A cross-version extension can preserve `constraint` when downgrading to R4, but that is not a base R6 design alternative to a breaking change.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 preservation may require extensions, but that is downgrade mitigation rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R6 defines SearchParameter.constraint as 0..1 string.
R4 has no SearchParameter.constraint element.
Local package count found one R6 core SearchParameter with constraint (`example-constraint`).

examples.examplesMd: Ignoring the R6 `constraint` may produce a syntactically usable R4 SearchParameter, but not one with the same applicability semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 can now say that a SearchParameter is applicable only under an additional FHIRPath condition. That is important executable metadata, not just documentation. R4 has no standard slot for it.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: no break. R6-to-R4: the `constraint` element is not representable in the R4 base resource. A strict R4 parser rejects it; a lenient parser that drops it changes behavior.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, preserve `constraint` in an extension or avoid publishing the SearchParameter through R4 unless the applicability rule can be enforced elsewhere. Add tests that exercise resources satisfying and not satisfying the constraint.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An R4 extension would have been the only backward-compatible vehicle. Adding the element to R6 is appropriate for base interoperability, but it necessarily requires downgrade policy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds an optional `constraint` string to describe conditional applicability of a SearchParameter. Because the element is optional and absent from R4, it does not invalidate R4 instances in R6. An R4 consumer downgrading R6 metadata may ignore or lose the condition, but that is a reverse-direction capability loss, not a design problem for R4-to-R6 compatibility.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition defines `SearchParameter.constraint` as 0..1 string.
R4 StructureDefinition has no `SearchParameter.constraint` element.
Local R6 core package count found one SearchParameter using `constraint`: `example-constraint`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 does not make an optional additive element concerning absent a direct old-valid/new-invalid break or strong evidence of production reliance.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: older consumers may lose conditional applicability metadata, but R4 instances remain valid when moving to R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed. Publishing this only as an extension would help downgrades but would make the R6 condition less discoverable and less computable.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact framing; agree that no backwards-compatible alternative is applicable.

findings.title: R6 adds optional canonical metadata and alias fields not present in R4

affectedLocation.newPath: SearchParameter.identifier / versionAlgorithm[x] / title / copyright / copyrightLabel / aliasCode
affectedLocation.newElementId: SearchParameter.identifier; SearchParameter.versionAlgorithm[x]; SearchParameter.title; SearchParameter.copyright; SearchParameter.copyrightLabel; SearchParameter.aliasCode

oldState.summary: R4 SearchParameter lacked these local elements; comparable information required extensions, narrative, or external governance.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 already had canonical `url`, `version`, `name`, publisher/contact, and purpose metadata, but not these additional identity, display, version-ordering, copyright-label, or alias-code fields.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional metadata elements, several marked summary, and implements the CanonicalResource interface.
newState.narrativeMd: These fields improve publication metadata and backward-compatible naming, but they are R6-only in the base resource.

facts.newValue: R6 core SearchParameter examples used title in 5 resources and aliasCode in 2; identifier/versionAlgorithm/copyright/copyrightLabel were not used in core SearchParameter instances counted.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are optional additions, so they do not invalidate R4 data in R6. The compatibility risk is strict parsing/code generation and information loss when sending R6 definitions to R4 systems, especially for `aliasCode` and `versionAlgorithm[x]` because they can affect name migration and version selection behavior.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily conformance publication and client discovery metadata.

justification.inferredGoal: Align SearchParameter with richer canonical-resource publication metadata and support aliases for renamed parameters.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional canonical metadata additions preserve R4-to-R6 validity.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added metadata and alias elements are optional and align SearchParameter with richer canonical-resource publication needs. They do not make R4 instances invalid in R6, so extension/backport strategies are relevant only for downgrading R6 content to R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is required for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Publishing these concepts only as extensions would help R4 consumers preserve them, but it would reduce their discoverability and interoperability in R6 and is best viewed as a downgrade strategy.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 converters need extensions or accept metadata loss, but no old R4 instance is invalidated.

evidence.detail: R6 defines identifier, versionAlgorithm[x], title, copyright, copyrightLabel, and aliasCode.
R4 has no matching local elements.
Local package count found limited but real R6 core use of title and aliasCode.

examples.examplesMd: The example is syntactically valid R6 shape for the added fields, but an R4 representation would need extensions or would lose the metadata.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds several canonical publication and aliasing fields. This improves governance and migration support, but a strict R4 parser will reject those elements and a lossy converter will drop data that may matter for version comparison or old search-name compatibility.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: no hard break. R6-to-R4: each added field is outside the R4 StructureDefinition. Dropping `aliasCode` can lose backward-compatible renamed-parameter hints; dropping `versionAlgorithm[x]` can make version ordering ambiguous.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, define extensions for each added metadata field that must be preserved, especially `aliasCode` and `versionAlgorithm[x]`. Update generated R6 classes and summary serializers to include summary-marked new fields.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The compatible alternative was extension-only publication. Base-element addition is cleaner for R6 but requires explicit downgrade mapping.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional canonical-resource metadata such as `identifier`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `title`, copyright fields, and `aliasCode`. These additions do not reject any R4 SearchParameter instance. R6-to-R4 conversion may need extensions or may drop metadata, especially aliases, but this is ordinary additive metadata evolution rather than a problematic base break.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition defines optional `identifier`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `title`, `copyright`, `copyrightLabel`, and `aliasCode` elements.
R4 StructureDefinition has no matching local elements.
Local R6 core package has limited use: `aliasCode` on 2 SearchParameters and `title` on 5; no `versionAlgorithm[x]` use was found.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 warrants noting downgrade loss, but additive optional metadata does not create enough compatibility pressure for Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling and R6-to-R4 loss: R6 metadata may not round-trip to R4, but old R4 instances remain valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is required. Keeping these concepts extension-only would be more compatible for R4 consumers but less interoperable and discoverable for R6 tooling.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact framing; agree that no backwards-compatible alternative is applicable.

findings.title: R6 gives SearchParameter.chain special wildcard, unlimited, and dotted-path semantics

oldState.summary: R4 described chain as names of search parameters that may be chained, drawn from SearchParameter.code on the target resource type.

semanticText.comment: Systems are not required to list all the chain names they support, but if they don't list them, clients might not know to use them.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 chain values were documented as search parameter names, without special wildcard or trailing-dot syntax in the StructureDefinition text.

newState.summary: R6 comments define `*`, trailing `.`, and dotted chain paths as meaningful chain declarations.

semanticText.comment: A single chain value of '*' means all reference search types supported can be chained; a value ending in '.' indicates unlimited chaining beneath it; dotted paths enumerate specific chaining paths.

newState.narrativeMd: The string field is unchanged, but some string values now have standardized semantics that an R4-era client may treat as literal names.

facts.oldValue: Contains the names of any search parameters which may be chained...
facts.newValue: Notes define '*', name ending '.', and dotted chain paths.
Local R6 core package count found no special chain values among core SearchParameter instances, but the StructureDefinition permits the semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No R4 instance becomes structurally invalid because the element remains a string. The risk is semantic/runtime: R6 chain values such as `*` or `practitioner.` are syntactically acceptable in R4 but do not have the same documented meaning there, so old clients may misinterpret chain support.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The impact is client search planning and conformance interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Compactly express broad or recursive chaining support without enumerating every chain.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 validation; `chain` remains a string and old instances remain structurally valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of compactly declaring wildcard, recursive, and dotted chain support is reasonable, and the element shape does not create a hard R4-to-R6 validation break. The main risk is semantic interpretation when R6 declarations are consumed by R4-era clients. That makes the backwards-compatible alternative question not applicable under the R4-to-R6 base-break calibration, even though the design still has downgrade ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Separate optional fields for wildcard and recursive chaining could be clearer, but because this finding is mainly about new R6 semantics on an unchanged string element, that is a modeling and downgrade alternative rather than a backwards-compatible alternative to an R4-to-R6 validation break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 semantic downgrades may require enumeration or extensions because old clients can misread special chain values.

evidence.detail: R4 says systems need not list all chain names but does not define wildcard/trailing-dot semantics.
R6 comment defines `*`, trailing `.`, and dotted chaining paths.
Local package count found no core R6 SearchParameter using special chain syntax, so prevalence outside examples is unknown.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can carry these strings, but not with the standardized R6 meanings; this is semantic rather than structural non-representability.

findings.narrativeMd: The same `chain` element now carries richer conformance semantics. A cross-version converter that merely preserves the strings may still mislead R4 clients because `*` and trailing-dot syntax are not just ordinary chain names in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No hard validation break: the field is still `0..* string`. R6-to-R4 semantic compatibility is the issue. R4 clients may treat `*` or `practitioner.` as literal parameter names or reject them by policy.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When downgrading to R4, either omit special chain declarations, translate them to explicit enumerated chain names when possible, or preserve them in an extension with clear documentation. Add client tests for wildcard and recursive chain declarations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 design could have used separate structured metadata for wildcard and recursive behavior. That would avoid overloading string values but would add more elements and still require R4 extensions for downgrade.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `SearchParameter.chain` remains a repeatable string, and R6 adds documented meanings for `*`, trailing `.`, and dotted chain paths. Existing R4 chain values remain structurally valid. An R4-era client could misread an R6 declaration using the new conventions, but the local R6 core package does not use those special syntaxes, and the issue is primarily new semantic expressiveness in the reverse direction.
keyEvidence: R4 `SearchParameter.chain` is 0..* string with prose saying systems need not list all chain names.
R6 `SearchParameter.chain` is still 0..* string and its comment defines wildcard, unlimited chaining, and dotted path forms.
Local R6 core package count found no SearchParameter using `*`, trailing `.`, or dotted chain syntax.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 supports documenting the semantic change, but the unchanged wire shape and lack of observed core usage keep this below a standards-revisit threshold.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: R6 gives special meanings to some string values, creating possible R6-to-R4 interpretation loss but no old-valid/new-invalid break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Separate fields for wildcard or recursive chaining could make R6 semantics clearer, but that would be a modeling alternative for new functionality, not a less-breaking design needed to preserve R4 instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing no-hard-break and Not applicable alternative assessment; disagree with treating the practical runtime/R6-to-R4 risk as Medium.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag match. Status/maturity changed and are recorded as notable non-breaking changes.
For local elements present in both R4 and R6, no min/max cardinality changes were found. Material presence changes are reported separately as additions/removals.
For local elements present in both versions, the datatype shapes were stable. New choice/type domains such as `versionAlgorithm[x]` and `type=resource` are covered in findings.
`SearchParameter.derivedFrom` and `SearchParameter.component.definition` remain canonical references targeting SearchParameter.
No fixed, pattern, or default values were found on local SearchParameter elements in either StructureDefinition.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were found except explicit local invariants reported as findings.
Existing local modifier status is stable: `SearchParameter.status` remains a modifier and the other common local elements remain non-modifier.
Existing common local summary flags are stable. Several added R6 metadata fields are summary elements and are covered in the R6-only metadata finding.
No local slicing changes were identified in the SearchParameter StructureDefinition.
PublicationStatus and SearchComparator code systems had unchanged code sets in the local packages. Material binding changes for modifier, type, base, and target are reported separately.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Maturity metadata changed from trial-use/FMM 3 to normative/FMM 5
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical artifact identity and instance wire format are not changed by maturity metadata alone.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and dependency policies may treat the R6 SearchParameter definition as more stable, but this does not by itself require instance transformation.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 declares implementation of CanonicalResource
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The declaration does not change the resource type or baseDefinition; the concrete added elements are covered separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators may expose SearchParameter through a CanonicalResource interface in R6 even though R4 used only a codegen-super extension for MetadataResource-like behavior.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Jurisdiction binding moved to terminology.hl7.org and R6 recommends useContext for jurisdiction
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element cardinality, type, and extensible binding strength are unchanged; this is not a hard base validation break based on the supplied definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: New content should consider representing jurisdiction through `useContext` as recommended by the R6 comment. Terminology details should be checked with an expansion service for profile-specific validation.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds meaningWhenMissing guidance for experimental, multipleOr, and multipleAnd
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: No cardinality or type changed, and absent values remain syntactically allowed.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Runtime logic should align with R6 defaults: absent `experimental` means not experimental; absent `multipleOr` or `multipleAnd` leaves support to server discretion.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds or changes warning-level canonical/name constraints
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `cnl-1` on url and `cnl-0` on name are warnings, not error-level validation failures in the supplied StructureDefinition.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Quality gates that treat warnings as failures should check URLs for `|`, `#`, or spaces and names for R6 canonical naming expectations.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited element, constraint, and narrative changes on `Resource`/`DomainResource` appear in the SearchParameter snapshot but are intentionally excluded from local findings.
Changes to base `ele-1`, extension constraints, and backbone extension behavior should be assessed by the assigned base artifact reports, not duplicated here.
The `base`/`target` finding depends on exact resource-type expansions and on resource-specific removal/rename analyses for codes absent from the local R6 value set.
A formal map would improve migrations for `xpath`/`xpathUsage` to `processingMode`, `ofType` to `of-type`, and R6-only metadata fields.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or ballot change log was used, so justification and backward-compatible alternative assessments are inferred from computable definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official HL7 change proposals, Jira tickets, or published diff pages for SearchParameter.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparisons used local CodeSystem concepts and ValueSet compose statements, not an authoritative terminology-server expansion. This is most important for `version-independent-all-resource-types` and `search-modifier-all-codes`.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run both R4 and R6 bindings through the same terminology server and compare full expansions, including inactive concepts and supplements.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is ballot build `6.0.0-ballot4`, not a final published release. Some details may change before final R6 publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Repeat the analysis against the final R6 core package when available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Prevalence statements count only local core package SearchParameter resources. They do not estimate custom IG or production registry usage.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Scan representative implementation guides and production SearchParameter registries.
